author: rdc-rfc1-author-c (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: A source-only reset clears a high stb_a_q, and the active consumer detects that as a strobe toggle and loads the reset command into applied_b_o, a command the producer never sent.

author_reading.rationale: A strobe toggle caused by the source reset can make the consumer apply the reset value of the command register. Whether that value is a no-op depends on the command encoding and a software quiesce protocol that the RTL and SDC do not state.

labels.rationale: The toggle synchroniser's source toggle stb_a_q is reset by rst_a_n, and its detector stages by rst_b_n. A one-sided reset can create a spurious edge in the destination, so applied_b_o loads a stale or zero command.
When a source reset clears a high strobe, the still-active consumer interprets that transition as another command. The detector also uses the first synchroniser stage directly.
labels.suspected_flaw: RDC-023 requires a recognised detector after the first stage. This case uses an early-stage XOR.

settlement.rationale: Both readers are right on bad, critical and class. A's RDC-023 (toggle synchroniser with mismatched resets) and RDC-005 (both) target the spurious event. The author's unknown is not upheld: whatever the encoding, the consumer's applied command changes nondeterministically on a source reset. Sites merge both readers.
